newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Dead Romanian babies stored to save burial expense.
newsitem.headline: Dead Romanian babies stored to save burial expense.

text.p: Doctors at a Romanian hospital said on Monday they were storing the corpses of 15 dead babies in a chemical solution because they could not afford to bury them.
The doctors, in the central city of Cluj, denied media reports alleging the existence of a mass grave for abandoned children who died at their paediatrics ward.
They said the cash-strapped hospital kept the autopsied corpses of 15 children in formalin, a solution of formaldehyde in water, because they could not pay for their burial.
"We preserve the bodies of the dead children in a formalin bath, waiting for their parents to show up and claim them," paediatrics hospital director Ioan Figan told Reuters by telephone from Cluj.
"This is a normal procedure for unclaimed bodies," Figan said, dismissing the mass grave reports as "sheer fantasy".

Local health authorities, faced with growing popular discontent over the crumbling medical care system, have pledged to find a quick answer to the problem of the dead babies, aged between one month and two years, abandoned at the Cluj hospital.
Plummeting living standards in the post-communist era have forced many Romanian couples to abandon their children.
